questions.text: Which of the following is not a maturity level as per Capability Maturity Model?
questions.solution:
CMM levels: Initial, Repeatable, Defined, Managed, Optimizing. "Measurable" is not one of them.

Answer: Measurable

questions.text:
Consider the following pseudo- code
 while (m < n)
    if (x > y) and (a < b) then
        a=a+1
        y=y-1
    end if
m=m+1 end while
What is cyclomatic complexity of the above pseudo -code?
questions.solution:
Cyclomatic complexity = number of simple conditions + 1.

- while (m [latex]\lt[/latex] n): 1
- if (x [latex]\gt[/latex] y) and (a [latex]\lt[/latex] b): 2 conditions

V = 3 + 1 = 4

Answer: 4

questions.text: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
questions.solution:
Good modules do one job well (high cohesion) and depend little on other modules (low coupling).

Answer: High cohesion and low coupling

questions.text: Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- The requirements document says what the system should do, not how it is implemented.
- Complete and consistent requirements are rarely achieved in practice.
- Prototyping lets users check the requirements early, so it is a requirements validation technique [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Requirements review finds errors in the requirements, not in the design.

Answer: Prototyping is a method of requirements validation
